title: A workflow file
summary: A workflow describes jobs GitHub Actions can run for a repository. The YAML file lives under .github/workflows.
introduction: A workflow describes jobs GitHub Actions can run for a repository. The YAML file lives under .github/workflows. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A workflow describes jobs GitHub Actions can run for a repository. The YAML file lives under .github/workflows.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Examples are YAML fragments or complete files as stated. Reading needs no account. Running them is a separate action in a permitted GitHub repository and may use hosted minutes.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of GitHub Actions. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
name: Say hello
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  hello:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Hello, club"
blocks.title: A workflow file

blocks.text: This workflow has a manual trigger, one job and one shell step. Reading the file does not run it.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Name the file hello.yml and point to its trigger.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Running hosted workflows uses the service's permissions and usage rules; no run is needed to read this course.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub Actions further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/actions).
